deliverables.text: A labeled 2x2 regional technical coefficient matrix A (Appendix B), every entry defined in words, with the matrix's dimensions stated.
The identity matrix I and the computed matrix (I - A), with every entry shown as an arithmetic step.
The determinant of (I - A), computed by hand using the 2x2 determinant formula, with an explanation of why a nonzero determinant matters.
The solved total-regional-jobs vector x = (I - A)^-1 d for each employer's direct-jobs vector d, with full matrix arithmetic shown.
A final decision table: direct jobs, total regional jobs supported, incentive dollars owed, and jobs supported per $10,000 of incentive, for both employers, with a stated recommendation.

appendices.title: Calder County's Regional Technical Coefficient Matrix

balance.argument_a: Meridian Forgeworks (140 direct jobs) solves to 191.62 total regional jobs supported (multiplier 1.369) for a $420,000 incentive -- 4.5624 jobs per $10,000 of incentive.
balance.argument_b: Cascade Distribution (310 direct jobs, more than double Meridian's headcount) solves to 368.02 total regional jobs supported (multiplier 1.187) for a $930,000 incentive -- 3.9572 jobs per $10,000 of incentive. Cascade still creates far more total regional jobs in absolute terms; it only loses on the per-incentive-dollar metric.
balance.margin_basis: Compare jobs-supported-per-$10,000-of-incentive: (4.5624 - 3.9572) / 4.5624 = 13.27%. Both bids pay an identical $3,000/job flat rate, so the entire margin comes from the two sectors' different local-purchasing multipliers (1.369 vs 1.187), not from the incentive rate itself.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Calder County's regional technical coefficient matrix A (Appendix B)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Calder County is fictional, so no purchased RIMS II table exists for it; a real county's own table costs $520 (Appendix C, S1) and was not purchased for this exercise. These four values were chosen so the resulting Sector-1 and Sector-2 output multipliers (1.369 and 1.187) land within a few hundredths of BEA's own real, published Type I multiplier examples for a real county -- Butler County, OH: 1.3616 (manufacturing) and 1.1810 (a comparison service industry) -- and preserve the real, sourced direction that manufacturing carries a higher local multiplier than trade/distribution in a county-sized region (Appendix C, S2).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The case's entire primary-metric margin depends on these four numbers. A different real county's own purchased RIMS II table would give different exact multipliers -- that dependency is disclosed here, not hidden.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Calder County's flat incentive rate, $3,000 per net new direct job (Appendix D)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Anchored to Florida's real Qualified Target Industry (QTI) Tax Refund base rate of $3,000 per net new full-time job under Section 288.106, Florida Statutes (Appendix F, S3). Calder County does not run Florida's actual QTI program; this case borrows its real base rate as a realistic flat-rate stand-in.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Because both bids are paid the same flat per-job rate, this rate cancels out of the comparison between A and B in relative terms -- raising or lowering it changes both incentive totals proportionally and does not by itself flip which option wins. It does change the absolute size of the jobs-per-$10,000 numbers in D5.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Direct job counts: Meridian Forgeworks 140; Cascade Distribution 310 (Appendix A)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Meridian Forgeworks and Cascade Distribution are both fictional companies invented for this case; there is no real employer to source their hiring plans from. The values were chosen to be realistic for a mid-size precision manufacturer and a regional distribution center respectively, and so Cascade's direct-jobs lead over Meridian (more than double) is large enough to make the naive 'more direct jobs wins' read genuinely tempting.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value, which is exactly why D5 asks you to compute the actual multiplier-adjusted comparison rather than compare the two headcounts directly.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: Calder County's technical coefficient a11 (MA1) is a good-faith estimate calibrated to real BEA RIMS II examples for a comparable real county (Appendix C, S2), because Calder County is fictional and no purchased RIMS II table exists for it; a +/-50% flex on this single coefficient can push the margin past the SPEC 2 20% cap without flipping which employer wins.

Calder County's technical coefficient a21 (MA1) is a good-faith estimate calibrated to real BEA RIMS II examples for a comparable real county (Appendix C, S2), same basis as a11; a +50% flex can push the margin to exactly the SPEC 2 20% cap boundary.

Calder County's technical coefficient a22 (MA1) is a good-faith estimate calibrated to real BEA RIMS II examples for a comparable real county (Appendix C, S2), same basis as a11; a -50% flex can push the margin past the SPEC 2 20% cap without flipping which employer wins.
